messages:
sre-bot: [ALERT] apiserver 5xx rate increased to 22% in eu-central-1, leader-election flaps detected
anya: I see the same on dashboards, started ~12:10 UTC, lots of watch errors
devon: no prod deploys. controller-manager restarted twice around 12:11
raj: logs show watch backlog + etcd timeouts, suspect control-plane egress saturation
kyle: running quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n kube-system | egrep 'apiserver|controller'` -> multiple restarts on controller-manager and apiserver OOMKill on one replica
marie: paste: ```E0317 12:11:45.987 handler.go:98] watch closed: etcdserver: request timed out
E0317 12:12:02.123 etcd.go:45] grpc: the connection is unavailable```
anya: coincident with a customer GPU attach spike — saw ~60 attach ops/min in eu-central-1 from scheduled batch jobs
raj: attach loops create heavy NAT conntrack churn on control-plane path, we've hit conntrack high watermark before
devon: can we check conntrack metrics on the NAT instances?
kyle: `sum(conntrack_entries{region="eu-central-1"}) = 410000` — nearing sysctl max, SYN drops around 12:09
sam: infra confirmed NAT host conntrack counters and kernel dropped packets at 12:08, scaling NAT pool now
ops-bot: mitigation applied: provisioner attach rate limiter enabled for eu-central-1 (10m)
anya: short-term playbook idea: 1) bump conntrack_max on NAT nodes 2) spin up extra NAT gateways 3) apply provisioner-side attach throttles 4) rolling restart one apiserver to re-establish healthy watch streams
marie: agreed. I can restart one apiserver replica with reduced `--max-requests-inflight=800` as a canary
raj: controller-manager leader election timeouts were tight, recommend +1s lease duration to reduce thrash during transient latency
devon: caution: increasing conntrack_max will increase kernel memory usage; infra to monitor memory and page alloc
sam: infra will add 2x temporary NAT gateways and monitor conntrack/mem, applying conntrack_max=524288 for now
kyle: also added a dashboard panel for conntrack headroom and NAT packet drops, linking to runbook
anya: early signal: apiserver 5xx dropped to ~6% after throttle and NAT scale, controller-manager restarts stopped
ops-bot: automated note: incident created INC-2026-047, status: mitigation in progress
marie: follow-ups: write a short postmortem, add automated autoscale for NAT pool when conntrack > 70% for 2m, and add per-customer attach soft-limits in provisioner
raj: medium-term: consider regional dedicated egress appliances or per-region control-plane egress isolation to avoid multi-tenant blast radius
devon: also add circuit-breaker in provisioner to back off attach retries exponentially when we see etcd/kv latency > 200ms
anya: staying on this feed for 30m to confirm stability, will escalate if regressions. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident updated: mitigation successful, monitoring for regressions (next update in 10m)
